key_insight: This paper shows that an integrated machine-learning framework for liquid electrolyte design can be reused and extended effectively across systems. The study finds that data size and composition strongly influence robustness, and that the framework improves cross-system transfer and multiscale performance over baselines.
problem_solved: Designing liquid electrolytes is difficult because models often do not transfer well across different chemistries, scales, or data regimes. This work addresses the need for a reusable, extensible framework that remains reliable when applied to new electrolyte systems and limited or shifting datasets.
method: Extended a unified modelling framework for liquid electrolyte design to test reuse across multiple settings.
Evaluated how training data size and composition affect model robustness and generalization.
Compared performance against baseline approaches on cross-system transfer and multiscale prediction tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper highlights how to build models that are not just accurate in one setting but adaptable across related domains. It offers practical guidance on dataset composition and transferability, which is especially valuable for scientific machine learning and materials discovery.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing the integrated electrolyte-design workflow from data to prediction to evaluation.
A robustness chart comparing performance across different dataset sizes and compositions.
A transferability matrix illustrating source-system to target-system generalization.
An icon-based comparison of baseline models versus the proposed framework across single-scale and multiscale tasks.
paper_title: Reusability report: Exploring the utility and extensibility of an integrated modelling framework for liquid electrolyte design
paper_authors: Genming Lai, Juntao Zhao, Zekai Liu, Ruiqi Zhang, Hanming Li
